subcategory: species shrub rose grown for foliage

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container specimens in early spring or fall once soil is workable, spacing plants to allow air circulation around the arching canes.

directions: Set plants in well-drained soil amended with compost, in a spot with at least six hours of sun, and water deeply during the first growing season to establish a strong root system. Prune only lightly in late winter to shape the arching canes, since flowers form on both old and new wood. This species rose is grown chiefly for its plum-purple to blue-gray foliage on wine-red stems, with small single pink flowers in late spring followed by showy orange-red hips that persist into winter. It tolerates partial shade and poor soil better than most garden roses, making it a striking hedge or background plant.

subcategory: species shrub rose grown for hips

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container specimens in early spring once the ground can be worked, giving the shrub ample room to develop its large mature size.

directions: Choose a permanent site with full sun and good drainage, since this vigorous species rose grows into a large arching shrub that resents transplanting once established. Water regularly the first year and mulch to conserve moisture, then reduce supplemental watering as the deep roots mature. Deep crimson, single five-petaled flowers appear along the canes in early summer, followed by an outstanding display of large, flagon-shaped orange-red hips in fall that persist well into winter. It is best used as a specimen or background shrub where its size and structural form have room to shine.

common_name: Father Hugo Rose (Golden Rose of China)
subcategory: species shrub rose, early spring bloomer

planting.note: Set container or bare-root plants in early spring in well-drained soil, spacing widely to accommodate the shrub's fountain-like mature form.

directions: Plant in full sun with good air circulation and well-drained soil, watering deeply while roots establish and then relying mostly on natural rainfall. Prune only to remove dead or crossing wood right after flowering, since blooms form on the previous year's growth. This is one of the earliest roses to flower each year, covering its arching, fern-like foliage with pale yellow single blooms in mid-spring before most other roses have even leafed out. Small dark hips follow in fall, and the fine-textured foliage gives the shrub an airy, graceful habit distinct from typical garden roses.

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container plants in spring, spacing to allow trailing canes to spread and root as they touch the ground.

directions: Plant in full sun on a bank, slope, or open bed where the trailing stems can spread and root at the nodes, and water regularly only until plants are established. Once rooted, it tolerates dry, sandy soil and needs little supplemental irrigation, making it useful for erosion control. Clusters of small, fragrant white single flowers with bright yellow centers open in mid to late summer, later than most other roses, followed by small red hips. Its glossy, nearly evergreen foliage and low, spreading habit make it more of a groundcover than an upright shrub, and it is a parent species of many popular rambling roses.

common_name: Sunny Knock Out Rose (Yellow Knock Out)
subcategory: landscape shrub rose, Knock Out series

planting.note: Transplant container-grown plants in spring after the last hard freeze, into well-drained soil with room for the shrub's mature rounded form.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained soil, watering deeply during the first season and then only during dry spells once established. Light shearing in late winter keeps the rounded shrub form tidy and encourages fresh bloom flushes through the season. Single, bright yellow flowers that fade to creamy white open continuously from spring to frost on this low-maintenance landscape shrub, part of the widely planted Knock Out series bred for disease resistance and repeat bloom without deadheading. Its compact size and self-cleaning flowers make it popular for mass plantings and foundation beds.

subcategory: landscape shrub rose, Knock Out series

planting.note: Transplant container-grown plants in spring once frost danger has passed, spacing to allow good air movement around the mature shrub.

directions: Set plants in full sun with well-drained, fertile soil, watering consistently the first year to establish a deep root system. An occasional light pruning in late winter maintains a compact, well-branched shape and promotes vigorous new flowering wood. Single, coral-orange blooms with a lighter reverse open in flushes from late spring through fall on this compact member of the Knock Out series, bred for strong disease resistance and minimal care. The warm coral tone stands out among the more common red and pink Knock Out selections, and plants rebloom reliably without deadheading.

planting.note: Transplant container-grown plants in spring into well-drained soil, spacing closely for a continuous low border or mass planting.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained soil, watering regularly the first season and reducing frequency once the compact root system is established. Prune back by roughly a third in late winter to keep the mounded habit dense and encourage abundant new flowering shoots. Double, peach-to-coral blooms that fade to soft pink open in large clusters over low, spreading mounds of small glossy foliage, part of the Drift series developed by crossing groundcover and miniature roses. Its diminutive size and long bloom season from late spring to frost make it well suited to container plantings, rock gardens, and small-space borders.

planting.note: Transplant container-grown plants in spring into well-drained soil, spacing closely to form a continuous low groundcover.

directions: Set plants in full sun with good drainage, watering deeply during establishment and only occasionally afterward thanks to the shrub's compact, drought-tolerant root system. A light shearing in late winter keeps the low mound shape neat and stimulates fresh bloom cycles. Semi-double coral-orange flowers with hints of yellow at the base cover the small, dense mounds of foliage from late spring through frost, a hallmark of the Drift series bred for continuous bloom and reduced disease susceptibility compared to older groundcover roses. It works well cascading over walls or spilling from raised beds and containers.

subcategory: groundcover shrub rose, Flower Carpet series

planting.note: Transplant container-grown plants in spring into well-drained soil, spacing to let the wide-spreading mounds knit together into a solid groundcover.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained soil, watering deeply through the first growing season to encourage roots to spread beneath the wide, low canopy. Once established, the vigorous, disease-resistant foliage needs little care beyond an annual cutback in late winter to renew growth. Small, bright pink semi-double flowers smother the spreading mounds almost continuously from late spring to frost, a signature trait of the original Flower Carpet introduction that popularized low-maintenance groundcover roses. Its dense habit suppresses weeds and works well on slopes, in mass plantings, or cascading over retaining walls.

common_name: Munstead Wood Rose (David Austin English Shrub Rose)

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container roses in early spring or fall in soil enriched with compost, spacing to give the rounded shrub room to fill out.

directions: Set plants in full sun with at least six hours of direct light and rich, well-drained soil, watering deeply and regularly during the first year to build a strong root system. Prune back by about a third in late winter and remove spent blooms through the season to encourage repeat flowering. Deep crimson, richly fragrant double blooms with an old-rose form open in flushes from early summer to frost on this compact, bushy English shrub rose. Its dark, velvety petal color and strong scent make it a standout among David Austin's English rose introductions for borders and cutting gardens.
